clue.text: Stare stupidly at wrecks originally entered in Grand Prix

indicators.note: the opening letters are said to go inside the racing abbreviation

parts.note: GP is the standard abbreviation for a Grand Prix motor race

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words at and wrecks

explanation.surface: A spectator gapes at the crashed cars in a Formula One race.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is a British colloquial verb for gazing open-mouthed in a foolish way.

clue.text: Backing cultural pursuits, they must include Spanish dance

indicators.note: backing means the word for cultural pursuits is read from the end

parts.note: the arts are cultural pursuits

indicators.note: must include tells us the pronoun has the Spanish abbreviation placed within it

parts.note: taken as written
Sp is a standard abbreviation for Spanish

explanation.surface: Patrons of the arts are told a Spanish dance must feature in their programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' gives STRA and 'must include' gives THESPY. 'Spanish dance' reads as one phrase, but Spanish belongs to the wordplay; a strathspey is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish country dance, a close relative of the reel.

clue.text: Like stomachache, maybe, one nursed by poor old bald man

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside, so the numeral letter is cradled by the jumbled letters
poor signals that the letters of the following words are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A poor old bald man looks after someone with a tummy ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the pool into ABDOMNAL before 'nursed by' adds the numeral; 'Like stomachache' is an adjectival definition, describing pain in the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomachache is a pain in the belly region, so it is an example of an abdominal complaint.

clue.text: Like thieves, it's said, displaying bovine impenetrability?

definitions.meaning: the saying 'as ... as thieves' describes very close friends
stupid, as dull as a cow, impossible to get anything through to

explanation.surface: Criminals are said to share the slow-witted obstinacy of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick means both intimately friendly, as in the idiom, and dim-witted or stupid.

clue.text: Work period given attention by a large number

parts.note: many means a large number
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A shift that a big crowd of people listens to carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is a unit of labour: the work one person does in a year.

clue.text: Tiny, disgusting tailless creepy-crawly

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for tiny

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word for disgusting is cut off

parts.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a small, revolting insect that has no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the E from VILE, leaving VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle, a typical example of a creepy-crawly or bug.

clue.text: Play's thread misconstrued among wealthy 33% or so

indicators.note: among says the jumbled word sits between the two other pieces

parts.note: rich means wealthy
a third is about 33 per cent

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich man misreads a storyline, taking about a third of it wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misconstrued' turns THREAD into ARDTHE, which goes 'among' RICH and THIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's history play about the hunchbacked king is usually written Richard III.

clue.text: Process of paying for establishment of Hanoverian succession?

definitions.meaning: settling a bill is paying it, so the deed of doing so
the 1701 English law that fixed the throne on the Protestant heirs of Sophia of Hanover

explanation.surface: A procedure for payment is set up to secure the Hanoverian line.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1701 Act of Settlement fixed the Protestant succession, bringing George I of Hanover to the British throne; literally, settling is paying.

clue.text: Mercury, perhaps — first of elements used in factory

indicators.note: used in means the single letter is put to work inside the works

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of elements

explanation.surface: Mercury as a chemical element is the first thing used in a manufacturing works.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury looks like the metallic element in a factory; it is the world nearest the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the smallest planet, the one closest to the Sun.

clue.text: One doesn't employ socially unacceptable son about to return

parts.note: non-U is the British label for language or behaviour not used by the upper class
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: to return means the short word for about is turned back

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone will not hire a boorish son who is coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns RE into ER. Non-U is the 1950s British term for not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-user is someone who does not use something, so one who doesn't employ it.

clue.text: Quiet about American Indian's first Asian dish

indicators.note: about means the hushing word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
US is short for American, as in United States

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Indian's

explanation.surface: A quiet American asks about the first Indian dish on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives SUSH and 'first' supplies the final letter; the possessive in Indian's is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so an Asian dish.

clue.text: Skilled verbalist, half poet, with German husband

indicators.note: half means only the front part of the poet's name is kept

parts.note: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A clever writer is half poet and has a German husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps WORDS from WORDSWORTH, the English Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsmith is someone skilled with language, a fluent writer.

clue.text: Basic pay finally accepted by subordinate

indicators.note: accepted by means the letter is taken inside the word for subordinate

parts.note: an underling is a subordinate

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of pay

explanation.surface: A junior employee finally gets their pay accepted, which is fundamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives Y, which goes into UNDERLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlying means fundamental, lying beneath as the foundation, hence basic.

clue.text: Heading seen in sixteen letters?

definitions.meaning: at the head of, on top of
the alphabet from A through to P is sixteen letters

explanation.surface: A title appears among sixteen letters of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'A to P', the answer covers the first sixteen letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, so at the heading or head of something.

clue.text: Fowler, possibly, married girl kept by elderly relative

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the word for the old relative

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an elderly relative
Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A grandmother takes in a married girl, perhaps one keen on birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Fowler suggests a bird-catcher; it is H. W. Fowler, author of Modern English Usage.
explanation.definitionFit: H. W. Fowler wrote Modern English Usage, making him a famous expert on language rules.

clue.text: Increase one dimension of study in Mayfair?

parts.note: Mayfair is in the London postcode district W1, with the 1 read as I
a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Someone wants to enlarge one side of their study in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket area of central London with postcode W1; the digit is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to make broader, increasing the width, which is one dimension.

clue.text: Heavyweight woman with maids touring key area in Kent?

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the bride's letters encircle the key

parts.note: a bride is attended by bridesmaids
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A large woman and her attendants tour a significant district of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts BRIDE round G, giving BRIDGE. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a town in Kent, south-east England, so an area in that county.

clue.text: Sanction that hurt everyone at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for everyone comes at the front

parts.note: all means everyone
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone cries in pain after a punishment that applied to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' looks like a penalty, but here it is the verb for permitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to permit or authorise, the same as to allow.

clue.text: Temper regularly displayed in search for camp

indicators.note: displayed in means the chosen letters are shown inside the word for search

parts.note: a hunt is a search

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word temper

explanation.surface: Bad temper keeps showing during a search of the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks TME from Temper, which goes into HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hutment is an encampment of huts, as for soldiers, hence a camp.

clue.text: Simple office accommodating Italian quartet?

indicators.note: accommodating means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: prime is the church office said at the first hour of the day
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A plain office building houses four Italian musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' looks like a workplace but is the church service of Prime, one of the canonical hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means basic and unsophisticated, so simple.

clue.text: Agreement accepted by the old couple?

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the archaic form

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: An elderly couple accept a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' gives YE, as in Ye Olde Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke joins a pair of oxen, so it can mean a couple, a pair.

clue.text: Possible parasite upset Lincoln after a short time

indicators.note: after places the turned-up president's name behind the short time

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a short time

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Abe was US President Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: Lincoln is upset a moment later by a possible parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ABE into EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Some amoebas live parasitically in other creatures, so one is a possible parasite.

clue.text: Man's trendy, eating bread up in press chief's office

indicators.note: eating means taking the bread inside

parts.note: Ed's, a man's name with the possessive

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable man eats bread in the newspaper boss's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the Indian bread backwards for ITOR, and 'eating' sets it just after the first two letters of the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorship is the role of editor, the chief of a newspaper or press office.

clue.text: Accelerated reaction in sect a lady reformed

indicators.note: reformed means shaped again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In a religious sect, a lady who changes her ways speeds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalysed means caused a chemical reaction to speed up through a catalyst.

clue.text: Sort of accident familiar in rounders?

definitions.meaning: a road accident where the driver leaves the scene
rounders is a British bat-and-ball game where you strike and then dash for a base

explanation.surface: A kind of mishap often seen in a playground ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game similar to baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run accident is one where the driver flees; rounders players strike and sprint.

clue.text: Banker not at home — one with an eye for the birds?

definitions.text: one with an eye for the birds?

indicators.note: not means the word for at home is removed

parts.note: a financier is a banker
in means at home

explanation.surface: A banker out of the house is someone who likes looking at women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds' is British slang for young women, but here it is pigeons: a pigeon fancier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancier breeds or keeps birds, as a pigeon fancier, so has an eye for them.

clue.text: Male, 24, kept down by high-flyer

indicators.note: in a down clue, kept down by puts the saint below the bird

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a high-flying bird
24 down is the word saint, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: A male saint is kept down by a high-flying achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to 24 down, whose abbreviation ST goes under ERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it can stand for a male.

clue.text: Yellowy-brown marble associated with US city

parts.note: a taw is a large marble used for shooting
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A marble of a yellowish-brown colour comes from an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny is a warm orange-brown or yellowish-brown colour, like a lion.

clue.text: Virtuous type rested outside home

indicators.note: outside means the word for rested is placed round the other

parts.note: sat means rested
in means at home

explanation.surface: A good person took a rest outside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a very virtuous person, a model of goodness.

clue.text: Hairy man originally examining students at university?

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A shaggy man first examines students at university.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Esau was Jacob's twin, described as a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible calls Esau a hairy man, in contrast to his smooth brother Jacob.
